title: lowerPipelineWithLabels walks MultiStages back-to-front, breaking label-extraction-then-filter order
notes: lowerPipelineWithLabels (internal/logql/lower.go, lowerPipelineWithLabels's own MultiStages loop) walks a pipeline's stages strictly left-to-right in source order per LOGQL-PIPELINE-STAGE-ORDER, threading the growing `labelsExpr` forward so a stage occurring AFTER a label-extracting parser stage (`| json`, `| logfmt`, `| regexp`, `| unpack`) sees its extracted keys, while a stage occurring BEFORE it does not. This mutation reverses the iteration (`for i := len(e.MultiStages) - 1; i >= 0; i--`) so every pipeline's stages are visited back-to-front instead. Query used by the detector: `{job="api"} | logfmt | status > 400` (test/spec/logql/filter_numeric.txtar) — under CORRECT left-to-right order, `| logfmt` runs first and merges the extracted `status` key into labelsExpr, so `| status > 400` resolves it and correctly keeps only the two rows with status 500/503. Under the REVERSED mutant, `| status > 400` is lowered FIRST against the still-bare ResourceAttributes/LogAttributes columns (status is not a real column in either), so its presence probe is unconditionally false and the whole predicate degenerates to drop every row — a genuinely different, observably wrong result using actual supported LogQL syntax, not an invented shape. This is the label-mutation/filter-order case the grounding issue calls for: a query+dataset pair where swapping stage order changes labels/results, not merely the shape of an already-order-independent predicate. Two existing fixtures are already bound to the LOGQL-PIPELINE-STAGE-ORDER contract (BINDING-LOGQL-PIPELINE-STAGE-ORDER-FILTER-THEN-LINE over edge_label_filter_and_then_line_filter.txtar, and BINDING-LOGQL-PIPELINE-STAGE-ORDER-UNPACK-FORMAT over edge_multistage_filter_unpack_format.txtar) but neither actually depends on stage order: both compose two SQL predicate-only stages (or a predicate stage plus a post-fetch-only `| unpack`/`| line_format` pair with no SQL impact), so their ANDed predicates are order-commutative and verified NOT to change under this exact reversal mutation (checked by hand before selecting filter_numeric.txtar instead) — this is precisely the coverage gap LOGQL-PIPELINE-STAGE-ORDER's own blind_spots entry already names ("this contract's ordering claim rests entirely on the fixed TXTAR fixture set"), so filter_numeric.txtar's kill is new, real evidence for the labels-threading half of the contract, not a restatement of the two existing bindings. This mutation is scoped to internal/logql/lower.go (LogQL's own package-local pipeline loop) and does not touch internal/chsql/builder.go or any other head's lowering, so there is no shared-emitter/PromQL/TraceQL side effect to report here (unlike MUTANT-LOGQL-LABEL-MATCHER-UNANCHORED-1741's anchoredRegexPattern mutation). The detector needs no chdb build tag or live ClickHouse: the kill is a static sql/args/chplan text mismatch against test/spec/logql/filter_numeric.txtar's golden, reached before any chDB round-trip execution (internal/logql/lower_test.go's TestLower, no build tag). test/property/logql_test.go + test/property/oracle/logql/evaluator.go (this issue's other cited grounding) were evaluated as an alternative/additional detector and deliberately NOT used: the property/oracle shape roster (test/property/gen/shapes.go's logQLShapeRoster, referenced by LOGQL-STREAM-PIPELINE-PROPERTY-COVERAGE's own blind_spots) draws at most one pipeline stage per generated query and never composes a parser stage with a dependent label filter, so it cannot exercise this bug class at all today — adding that coverage is out of this change's scope (no wholesale local-oracle rewrite, no arbitrary stage permutations) and, if wanted, belongs in a separate filed issue rather than folded into this mutant record.
